newsitem.title: USA: Albright to State - I'm not Christopher.
newsitem.headline: Albright to State - I'm not Christopher.

text.p: With missionary zeal, the first woman U.S. Secretary of State, Madeleine Albright, seemed to impress applauding American diplomats during a get-acquainted session on Monday at the State Department.

"You may notice that I don't exactly look like Secretary (Warren) Christopher," she said, stepping from behind a podium and curtseying in her black dress before more than 800 employees who packed a department auditorium.
Beginning her first full week on the job, Albright said the hardest question asked during numerous recent interviews was how she felt about being a woman secretary of state.
"I have now thought of the answer," she said.
"I've never been a secretary of state before. I have been a woman for almost 60 years. Now we're going to see how we put the two together," she added.
Albright arguably revealed more about herself publicly in her half-hour appearance on Monday than her recent predecessors did in their entire terms of office.

-- "My appointment shows that the president of the United States is a believer that this country is a place where there is opportunity for all. I believe in diversity ... (and) will apply that principle to this department."

-- "I intend to use the bully pulpit of my office to spread the word that international affairs are not only relevant and interesting but exciting ... As part of this effort I hope we will strive in all of our public comunications for clarity and simplicity of language ... We don't need to speak down to the American people but we need to speak sense to them."

-- She renewed her promise to campaign vigorously for more funds to carry out diplomacy but also stressed the need to "rethink old habits ... and remember that our goal is not to spend time serving institutions but to make our institutions serve the times."
